title: Highland Sonnet of Nature (Ki Sonnet Ka Mariang)
cultural_context: Classical 14-line sonnet composed in iambic rhythm celebrating the geological majesty of the Khasi plateau, from 'Ka Tragoidia Bad Ki Poim'.

khasi: Haba nga ieng ha kliar Lum Kyllang,
Nga peit sawdong ia ka dur ka mariang;
Ki lyoh lieh ki her kum ki sniuh rupa,
Ha suin bneng ba jngum bad ba shai;
Ki wah kiba tuid kum ki ksai ksiar,
Ki pynim ia ki madan bad ki them;
Hangne ka dohnud ka sngewthuh kynjai
Ia ka burom ba la theh U Blei.
english: When I stand upon the granite dome of Mount Kyllang,
I gaze in wonder at nature's vast expanse;
White clouds drift like silken strands of silver,
Rivers flowing like threads of living gold,
Breathing vitality into plains and vales;
The divine majesty poured down by God.

khasi: Khlem ka bor briew, khlem ka jingthaw kti,
U Mawsiang Kyllang u ieng junom;
U iaineh ha pyrthei ba kylliang,
Kum ka dak jong ka hok ba skhem;
To ngin bat ia kane ka nongrim,
Ban im da ka akor ba kyntang,
Ba ka ri Khasi kan sah ba phyrnai
Kum u mawlynnai ha suin bneng.
english: Unaided by human power, unshaped by mortal hands,
The monolithic dome of Kyllang stands eternal;
Enduring through all shifting epochs of the world,
As an enduring emblem of immutable righteousness;
So let us cling to this holy foundation,
That the Khasi land may shine radiant
Like an unblemished jewel in the skies.

vocabulary.lum kyllang: Kyllang Rock (massive monolithic granite dome in West Khasi Hills)
